slides.title: How much of someone else do you actually let in?

body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
Role-Based Consecutive Touch vs Close Hand Game
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range. One is the touch player, one is the connection player.

Touch player: collect three touches in a row, a hand to the mat or a hand behind the knee, without letting the connection player close his hands on you. If he scores, your count goes back to zero. Connection player: close both hands around the touch player anywhere from armpits to ankles.

items: The touch player wins with three touches in a row.
The connection player wins with a closed-hand connection from armpits to ankles.

body.text: SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player has closed guard around the top player, who is on his knees inside, trying to open it.

Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player, connecting to his wrists, elbows, and head to make his hands touch the mat once. Top player: take your hands off the bottom player and get to your feet.

items: The bottom player wins by making the top player's hands touch the mat one time.
The top player wins by getting his hands off the bottom player and standing up.

body.text: SLO: Controlling for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest, both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
Top player: stay under the bottom player's elbows, keeping them away from his body. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your body, or make the top player fall over.

items: The top player has no time limit. He wins by keeping the elbows away from the body the whole time.
The bottom player wins by bringing both elbows to his body, or by making the top player fall.

slides.title: How you win it
slides.question: In Chest-to-Chest Elbow Control Game, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The top player has no time limit. He wins by keeping the elbows away from the body the whole time.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.

options.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
options.feedback: Never. Let go the instant your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.
You keep the pin by feeling your partner and moving with them, not by clamping down and squeezing hard. Staying calm beats forcing harder.

slides.correctText: That is how you win today.

body.text: Letting people in is like a dial you control. You just found yours.

Keeping a pin means feeling your partner and adjusting to them, not clamping down and ignoring them. Letting someone in works the same way. You hold the connection by reading the other person, not by shutting them out and pushing through alone.
